title: b1bc.8: DKIM signing in SmtpRelayQueue::try_deliver_one
description:
What: In crates/smtp/src/relay_queue.rs, insert DKIM signing between reading article bytes and calling deliver_via_relay inside try_deliver_one.

Algorithm (inside try_deliver_one, after article_bytes are loaded, before deliver_via_relay):
1. Check if self.dkim_signer is Some(signer):
   a. Call signer.sign(article_bytes) — returns Result<Signature, DkimSignError>.
   b. On Ok(sig): call sig.to_header() to get the full header line.
      Produce signed_bytes: Vec<u8> = header.as_bytes() + article_bytes.
   c. On Err(e): log error!('DKIM signing failed for article {}: {e}', message_id);
      Move article to dead-letter directory (permanent failure — never retry, never send unsigned).
      Return from try_deliver_one.
2. If self.dkim_signer is None, use original article_bytes as-is.
3. Call deliver_via_relay with the (possibly signed) bytes.

Note on failure semantics: NNTP path uses warn+continue (retry on next cycle). SMTP relay path uses error+dead-letter (permanent failure) because SMTP relay is a one-shot delivery with strict MTA expectations.

Defensive programming:
- Never deliver unsigned when dkim_signer is Some.
- error! log must NOT include message body.
- Dead-letter move uses existing dead-letter path logic in relay_queue.rs.
- No unwrap() in production path.

Tests (oracle: RFC 8463 test vectors):
- test_relay_dkim_signing_prepends_header: sign a known RFC 5322 test message; verify output starts with 'DKIM-Signature:'.
- test_relay_dkim_signing_absent: with dkim_signer=None, verify bytes are unchanged.
- test_relay_dkim_failure_dead_letters: with a mock signer that always fails, verify article is moved to dead-letter dir and NOT delivered.
